note: Adapted from the English species-level description in Bacchus (1997); the alate is recorded as Unknown in the original, so only the soldier and large worker can be described; the soldier section is taken here; measurements are taken from the first two rows of the measurement table (the ranges and type values in these two rows are self-consistent); the means are erroneous in the OCR and are not cited.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule and labrum yellow to orange, mandibles brown with yellow bases; antennae pale yellow, body and legs pale yellow to yellow; postmentum concolorous with the head, not darker than the genae. Head capsule short-oval, widest posteriorly, narrowing towards the antennal sockets; the difference between maximum head width and head width at the antennal bases 0.02—0.05 mm; sides of head with a few short to a few long setae, dorsal setae numerous and of unequal length, arranged symmetrically. Labrum broadly ligulate, extending over 0.65 of the mandible length, with 8—10 setae on the anterior half. Mandibles slender, apex slightly incurved, curvature 0.03—0.04 mm. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 shortest, segment 4 slightly longer, segment 1 longer than segment 2. Postmentum short and broad, posterior margin not V-shaped. Pronotum saddle-shaped, distinctly narrower than the head, lateral lobes sparsely setose, anterior margin with a narrow shallow median notch, posterior margin slightly concave, posterior part of lateral lobes rounded. Fore tibia weakly to moderately inflated; fore tibial spurs 3, the dorsal spur as long as the outer ventral spur. A seta on the fore coxa not spine-like. Measurements (14 heads, 7 colonies): head length (including mandibles) 1.10—1.23 mm (type 1.20 mm); head length to mandible base 0.70—0.75 mm (type 0.75 mm).
